grade.stack_chosen: Java 21 + Spring Boot 3 with virtual threads, blocking controller unchanged, plus Tomcat max-connections and accept-count raised
red_flags_hit: Ignoring cross-pod and cross-data-centre correlation of Kafka confirmations, which breaks once there is more than one replica
grade.notes: The agent found the real cause: Tomcat's 200-thread default. Its fix was minimal and on the approved stack (virtual threads, plus raising max-connections, accept-count, file-descriptor and memory limits), and it was honest that the code doesn't compile and hasn't been load-tested. It missed the OpenShift router's 30s timeout, the risk of running out of JDBC/pooled resources, virtual-thread pinning on Java 21, and routing Kafka confirmations to the pod that holds the request.
